messages:
sanjay: Heads up — we just got a DSAR delete that should have scrubbed embeddings from snapshots, but the erasure job failed on the eu-west snapshot copies. seeing KMS errors.

irene: oh no. any error codes? is the request under legal hold?

sanjay: no hold. user provided proof and it passed verification. error in worker logs: `KMS.DecryptAccessDenied: access denied for key alias/embeddings-eu-primary` on region eu-west-2. local region delete succeeded.

devon: that suggests cross-region key policy or IAM change. I pushed an RBAC tweak yesterday to service-account erasure-worker to restrict kms:Decrypt for non-primary regions.

maria: do we have audit log for that policy change?

audit-bot: policy-change recorded: actor=devon, iam_change=update_role(erasure-worker), time=1732004401, diff=removed kms:Decrypt on arn:aws:kms:eu-west-2:***:key/embeddings-eu

irene: can we prove that caused the DSAR miss? we need timeline and evidence for the requester and for legal.

devon: timeline: 1732004300 role update -> 1732004500 first failed erasure job. I can revert the role now if you want.

sanjay: revert now please. fallback plan is to re-run erasure against snapshots after rollback. need to confirm no other services rely on this tighter restriction.

maria: I'll pause the scheduled snapshot retention job to avoid further copies until we finish.

devon: rolling back role to previous policy in 2 mins. pushing change and will attach the exact policy diff.

devon: done. role restored. verifying...

sanjay: re-triggering the erasure worker on the failed snapshot job.

sanjay: worker log now shows success: `Erasure completed for snapshot s-2023-11-12-eu-west-2, 42 embeddings removed`

irene: good. please capture the successful run output and KMS audit entries for the deletion window. I'll prepare the DSAR response bundle. include the policy-change audit too.

maria: concerned about the change window — we should run a scan for other pending DSARs that hit eu-west snapshots between 1732004300 and 1732004800. I'll enqueue a quick query against the DSAR backlog table.

devon: adding a guardrail: new PR to enforce automated pre-deploy check that flags role changes which remove kms:Decrypt for `erasure-worker` scoped principals. will link PR.

sanjay: also recommend we add a metric/alert: erasure-job KMS.AccessDenied > 0 triggers paged pager during DSAR windows.

irene: for the DSAR reply: include apology, describe root cause (RBAC change inadvertently blocked eu-west KMS access), mitigation (immediate rollback + completed erasure), and evidence bundle (audit logs + post-fix erasure output). legal ok with that wording?

maria: legal reviewed quick draft and ok with explanation + timeline. they asked to log retention exception and note it as a near-miss in our privacy register.

devon: PR: https://git.internal/repo/infra/pulls/738 — adds predeploy check + unit tests.

sanjay: follow-ups: (1) add e2e test that simulates cross-region KMS denies for erasure; (2) run backlog scan and remediate any missed DSARs; (3) update runbook to include immediate rollback step and audit artifacts list.

irene: I'll prepare the DSAR response and set a 24h SLA to send it. assigning to legal+privacy.

maria: backlog scan found 2 DSARs in that window that touched eu-west snapshots — one already fixed by the rerun, one required manual scrub. both are now resolved.

audit-bot: evidence bundle created: s3://redwood-privacy/evidence/1732004567-bundle.zip (contains: policy-diff.txt, kms-audit.log, erasure-success.log, backlog-scan.csv)

sanjay: marking this thread resolved once PR merges and postmortem posted. thanks all. :pray:

irene: thanks — will add this to quarterly privacy review as an incident. :memo:
